# Judith Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_013_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Now when evening came, his servants quickly withdrew, and Bagoas closed the tent from outside and dismissed the attendants from the presence of his master. And they went to their beds, for they were all weary, because the banquet had been very long.

**2** But Judith was left alone in the tent, and Holofernes was lying on his bed, for he was overcome with wine.

**3** And Judith told her servant to stand outside the bedchamber and to wait for her to come out, just as she did every day. For she said she would go out for her prayer; and she had told this to Bagoas in the same words.

**4** And everyone withdrew from his presence, and no one, small or great, was left in the bedchamber. And Judith stood beside his bed and said in her heart, "O LORD God of all power, look in this hour upon the works of my hands for the exaltation of Jerusalem.

**5** For now is the time to aid your inheritance and to accomplish my purpose for the destruction of the enemies who have risen up against us."

**6** And she went to the bedpost that was by Holofernes' head and took down his sword from it.

**7** And she drew near to the bed and took hold of the hair of his head and said, "Strengthen me, O LORD God of Israel, this day."

**8** And she struck his neck twice with all her strength, and cut off his head from him.

**9** And she rolled his body off the bed and took down the canopy from the posts. And after a moment she went out and gave the head of Holofernes to her servant,

**10** and she threw it into her food bag. And the two of them went out together, as was their custom for prayer. And they passed through the camp and went around that valley and went up the mountain of Bethulia and came to its gates.

**11** And Judith called out from far off to the guards at the gates: "Open, open the gate! God — our God — is with us, still showing his power in Israel and his might against our enemies, just as he did today!"

**12** And it came to pass, when the men of her city heard her voice, they hurried down to the gate of the city and called together the elders of the city.

**13** And they all ran together, small and great, for her coming was unexpected; and they opened the gate and received them in, and lit a fire for light, and gathered around them.

**14** And she said to them with a loud voice: "Praise God — praise him! Praise God, who has not withdrawn his mercy from the house of Israel, but has destroyed our enemies by my hand this night!"

**15** And she brought out the head from the bag and showed it to them, and said: "Behold, the head of Holofernes, the commander of the Assyrian army, and behold the canopy under which he lay in his drunkenness. And the LORD struck him by the hand of a woman.

**16** As the LORD lives, who protected me in my way that I went, it was my face that deceived him to his destruction, and he did not commit sin with me to defile me and shame me."

**17** And all the people were greatly astonished and bowed themselves down and worshiped God, and said with one voice, "Blessed are you, our God, who this day have humiliated the enemies of your people."

**18** And Uzziah said to her, "Blessed are you, daughter, above all women upon the earth; and blessed be the LORD God, who created the heavens and the earth, who guided you to cut off the head of the chief of our enemies.

**19** For your hope will not depart from the hearts of men as they remember the power of God forever.

**20** May God make these things a perpetual exaltation to you, and visit you with blessings, because you did not spare your life when our people were brought low, but you acted against our fall, walking a straight path before our God." And all the people said, "Amen! Amen!"

---
*EMET notes: v. 8 — "twice" (dis) is precise and significant; she struck twice to sever the head. "With all her strength" renders en tē ischyi autēs. The double blow conveys physical effort — this is not effortless divine miracle but a woman doing a violent, difficult thing. v. 15 — "in his drunkenness" (en tē methē autou) is the author's explicit explanation of how this was possible. v. 16 — "my face deceived him" renders prosōpon mou ēpatēsen auton — the beautiful face was the instrument of judgment. v. 9 — "rolled his body off the bed" is precise and physical; the author does not spare the detail.*
